Cratylus ( / ˈ k r æ t ɪ l ə s / KRAT -il-əs ; Ancient Greek : Κρατύλος , Kratylos ) is the name of a dialogue by Plato . Most modern scholars agree that it was written mostly during Plato's so-called middle period. [ 1 ] In the dialogue, Socrates is asked by two men, Cratylus and Hermogenes , whether names are "conventional" or "natural", that is, whether language is a system of arbitrary signs or whether words have an intrinsic relation to the things they signify.
